prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Columbus after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a quick note: I can’t run a live web search from here, so I can’t produce a real‑time ranked list of Columbus firms. I can, however, tell you the best specific places and types of firms to call right away, why to call them, give a short script and exact questions to ask, and explain how to pick between any firms you find. If you want, give me your ZIP or the firm names you’re considering and I’ll help evaluate them.

Who to call first (specific places and why)
- Morgan & Morgan (Columbus office): national plaintiff firm with lots of resources, experienced trial lawyers, and a large personal‑injury practice — useful if your case needs substantial investigation or trial prep and you want a contingency arrangement.  
- Columbus Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (call or use their site): they’ll refer you to local attorneys with personal‑injury experience and provide basic screening to match your needs quickly. Good for finding vetted local specialists.  
- Ohio Association for Justice (OAJ) / Ohio Trial Lawyers listings: this organization lists plaintiff personal‑injury lawyers in Ohio; members often handle complex injury cases and trial work. Good for finding lawyers focused on plaintiffs’ rights.  
- Avvo / Martindale‑Hubbell / Google local search (look for Columbus personal injury/car accident attorneys with high ratings and recent reviews): these aggregate reviews and peer ratings that help identify active local firms and individual attorneys.

Why these options
- National firms (like Morgan & Morgan) bring resources for investigations, expert witnesses, and capacity to handle big claims or insurance companies.  
- Local specialist firms and OAJ members often have deep experience with Columbus/Franklin County judges, local discovery practices, and juries — helpful if the case goes to trial.  
- The Bar referral service speeds up vetting and gives you names of attorneys who actually handle car-accident PI work instead of generalists.

How to pick the right firms to call (call 3–4)
- Mix one large firm + 2–3 local/specialist firms. Compare responses, fees, litigation willingness, and chemistry.  
- Give priority to attorneys with: trial experience in personal injury, strong local track record, willingness to take the case on contingency, clear communication, and documented results (verdicts/settlements).

What to ask when you call (short script)
Intro: “Hi, I was in a car accident on [date]. I’m looking for a Columbus personal‑injury attorney. Do you handle car‑accident cases, and who would actually handle my case?”  
Key questions:
1. Do you take car‑accident injury cases on contingency? What percentage do you charge?  
2. Who will handle the case day‑to‑day — an attorney or paralegal/associate? Can I meet the lawyer now?  
3. How many car‑accident cases have you tried to verdict in Franklin County?  
4. What’s your experience with cases like mine (briefly describe injuries/insurance limits)?  
5. How do you handle medical/expenses advances and case costs?  
6. What’s your estimate for value/next steps and timeline?  
7. Can you provide references or recent verdicts/settlements?  
Red flags: promises of a specific payout, evasive answers about who will handle the work, inability to provide local trial experience, unclear fee structure.

Immediate actions while you choose a lawyer
- Get/keep medical treatment and copies of records.  
- Preserve evidence (photos, video, vehicle damage).  
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurers without talking to a lawyer.  
- Note names, badge numbers, and witness contacts.  
- Notify your insurer if required, but keep comments factual and brief.

If you want, I can:
- Help draft a brief description of your accident to use in intake calls.  
- Evaluate any specific firm names you find or give you a prioritized list based on details you provide (ZIP, severity of injuries, suspected fault/insurance amounts).  

Tell me your ZIP code or share any firm names you’ve already found and I’ll help you choose which to call first.
